Sermons on Morning Prayers: Now let us explain the general principles that lie in the order of the arrangement of the morning prayer. Know that from the beginning of the prayer until Barukh she-amar is the world of Asiyah; from Barukh she-amar until Yotzer or is the world of Yetzirah; from Yotzer or until the end of the blessing of the Patriarchs is the world of Beriah; and all the rest of the Amidah is the world of Atzilut. The order of Asiyah proceeds from below upward. And in order to unite Asiyah with Yetzirah — and behold, there are harsh and powerful kelipot in it — one must therefore first unite the head of Yetzirah with the head of Asiyah, and only afterward the remainder of Yetzirah, which proceeds from below upward; and so too Beriah proceeds from below upward. The blessing of the Patriarchs is the head of Beriah, called the Holy of Holies chamber of Beriah, up to the end of "Blessed are You, HaShem, Shield of Abraham," and all the rest of the Amidah is in Atzilut. And this is the explanation of all the foregoing: for the eighteen blessings from al netilat yadayim until the blessing over Torah are the eighteen blessings of the Yesod of Asiyah; and from Hodu until Barukh she-amar is the head of Asiyah, its Holy of Holies chamber; and Barukh she-amar is the Holy of Holies chamber, the head of Yetzirah — and therefore it contains thirteen occurrences of barukh, the numerical value of eḥad, and this is the secret of the thirteen measures of mercy that are in the world of Yetzirah. And therefore Barukh she-amar has eighty-seven words, according to the version we shall copy below, God willing, to hint that it is the head of Yetzirah, of which it is said "his head is finest gold (paz פ"ז, gm. 87)"; and therefore one must say ha-mehullal be-feh בפה amo — which comes to בפ"ה 87 in gematria — and not be-fi amo as it is written in the maḥzorim. And afterward come the eighteen Names contained in those verses from Yehi khevod HaShem le-olam until Tehillah le-David, as is known; and these are the eighteen blessings of the Yesod of Yetzirah. And since it is known that in each world of the four worlds ABiYA there are all ten sefirot and all the partzufim — namely Arikh Anpin, Abba and Imma, and Za and Nukva — therefore at the end of Yetzirah we again mention eighteen Names of Havayah in the Song at the Sea, and the thirteen praises of Yishtabaḥ, which are "song and praise, hallel and hymn," etc.

Now, when one is in the order of Asiyah, which is from the beginning of the prayer until Barukh she-amar as above, he should intend to raise all the nefashot that are there to the world of Yetzirah; and in the order of Yetzirah he should intend to raise all the ruḥin that are there to the world of Beriah; and in the order of Beriah he should intend to raise all the neshamot that are there to the world of Atzilut. Then the supernal Malkhut is comprised of all these nefashin, ruḥin, and nishmatin, and through this the aspect of mayin nukvin is made within her. And one must include himself as well, in all his parts — that is, to raise his nefesh together with the nefashot of Asiyah, his ruaḥ with the ruḥin of Yetzirah, and his neshamah with the nishmatin of Beriah; understand this well. And we have already explained the matter of the ascent of the worlds: that only the aspects of the nefashot, ruḥot, and neshamot within them ascend, but the worlds themselves do not ascend. Likewise, in the descent of the souls after the Amidah, you should include your nefesh, ruaḥ, and neshamah with them in the same manner as was said regarding the ascent. Further, know concerning the order of the Shaḥarit prayer: it has already been explained above that from the beginning of the eighteen blessings until Barukh she-amar is in the world of Asiyah; from there until Yotzer or, the world of Yetzirah; from there until the Amidah of eighteen, the world of Beriah; from there until the Kaddish said before Ashrei yoshvei, in Atzilut; and from Ashrei yoshvei until Tefillah le-David it returns to being the world of Beriah; and from there until Ein kadosh ka-HaShem it returns to being the world of Yetzirah; and from there until Aleinu le-shabeaḥ it is the world of Asiyah. And the intention is that one must first raise the worlds from below upward, as above, the lower world becoming bound to the world above it, until all the worlds together are found bound within the world of Atzilut at the time one prays the Amidah of eighteen — and then the supernal union takes place there. And afterward one must receive the supernal shefa drawn down from that union, and must lower it into the lower worlds from above downward. Therefore, when we say Ashrei yoshvei veitekha until Tefillah le-David, we are lowering the shefa from Atzilut to Beriah — the intention is not to lower the world of Beriah itself. And so likewise until Ein kadosh ka-HaShem ki ein biltekha, for then we are lowering the shefa from Yetzirah to Asiyah. And afterward, at Aleinu le-shabeaḥ, the aforementioned worlds descend, each one to its own place, as is written there, God willing. This has also been explained in [the discussion of] the psalm Ashrei yoshvei veitekha that is instituted after nefilat apayim, and it is set out there at whatever length is needed; see there carefully. Now, when you begin the aforementioned eighteen blessings up to Barukh she-amar, you should always direct your intention to the Tetragrammaton of the heh filling, which is in Asiyah and issues from the last heh of the all-inclusive Tetragrammaton, since it is known that the final heh is in Asiyah; and this Tetragrammaton of the heh filling is the secret of the soul of Asiyah, called the aspect of nefesh, and it is what ascends from its place to Yetzirah, as mentioned. You should also intend the Name El Adonai, which is in the world of Asiyah. And when you reach Barukh she-amar, until Yotzer or, intend the soul of the world of Yetzirah, which is the Tetragrammaton of the aleph filling, coming to forty-five, and it is the aspect of ruaḥ, as above; and also intend the Name El-YHVH, which is in the world of Yetzirah. And when you reach Yotzer or, until the Amidah, intend the soul of Beriah, which is the Tetragrammaton of the SaG filling; and also intend the Name El Shaddai, which is in the world of Beriah. And when you reach the blessing of the Patriarchs, after you have said "HaShem, open my lips," then intend the Tetragrammaton of the yod filling, which comes to seventy-two and issues from the yod of the all-inclusive Tetragrammaton — for you already know that "HaShem, open my lips" is in the Holy of Holies chamber of Beriah. And in precisely this same manner you should direct your intention at the time of the lowering of the three worlds after the Amidah, as above, until Aleinu le-shabeaḥ. And behold, it is not fitting to intend each one of them by itself, since the essence of the intention is to include and bind world to world. Therefore, when you reach Barukh she-amar, intend the lower heh of the Name YHVH, and intend the Name BaN of the heh filling; and also intend the Name El Adonai, and raise them and join them with the letter vav of the Name, and with the Name MaH of the aleph filling, and with the Name El-YHVH that is in Yetzirah. And when you reach Yotzer or, intend the lower heh, to raise it and cleave it to the letter vav, the vav being cleaved to the upper heh that is in Beriah; and likewise join the Name BaN of the hehs to the Name MaH, and the Name MaH to the Name SaG of Beriah; and likewise the Name El Adonai to the Name El-YHVH, and join them with the Name El Shaddai that is in Beriah. And when you reach the Amidah, intend to raise all four worlds, included one within another, in the three aspects mentioned, from below upward, in the manner described above. And in this same way you should do in reverse at the time of the descent of the worlds after the Amidah, as above. Thus it emerges that when you reach Ein kadosh ka-HaShem ki ein biltekha, etc., you should intend all four worlds, included one within another, from above downward.
Sermons on Passover: It is known that the Sages say that those early generations, namely, the generation of Enosh, [the generation of the Flood] and the generation of the Dispersion, caused the Shechinah to depart [and ascend] upward to the seventh firmament due to their sins. Know that the Israelites of the generation of the slavery in Egypt were the aspect of those drops of seed that Adam emitted during those 130 years before Seth was born, as the Sages said. Afterwards, they were reincarnated in the generation of the Flood, and therefore they also wasted their seed upon the ground, like the root from which they were formed and hewn out, until they were eradicated. This is what the verse says, “The Lord saw that the evil of the man (Ha’adam) was great upon the Earth” (Genesis 6:5), and it is known that wasting seed is called evil, and he who emits it is called evil, as the verse says, “Er, the firstborn of Yehuda, was evil in the eyes of the Lord” (Genesis 38:7), and it says, “Woe to the wicked [who does] evil” (Isaiah 3:11), and it says, “Evil shall not sojourn with You” (Psalms 5:5), as it is taught in the Zohar (Beresheet B verse 393). Thus, it is found that that generation was actually the evil of the known man, namely, Adam, the first man. This is what the verse says, “I will eradicate ‘the’ man whom I created” (Genesis 6:7), namely, Adam, the first man, himself, who was created by the hands of God Himself. These were his drops, and He wanted to eradicate them. Afterwards, these [drops] themselves were reincarnated in the generation of the Dispersion, regarding whom it is written, “The Lord came down to see the city and tower that the sons of the man (Ha’adam) had built” (Genesis 11:5). [This means] the sons of Adam, the first man; understand this. Therefore, they are called “the sons of the man” (lit. the sons of Adam), to allude that they were the drops of seed, and therefore, they were the sons of Adam, male without female. Also then, they continued to sin more, rebelling against the Most High, but they were not involved in the original sin of destroying seed like the generation of the Flood. You need to know that the concept of souls is analogous to the concept of gold that is formed in the belly of the Earth. When one extracts [gold from the earth], it is full of immeasurable amounts of dirt and dross, and it does not have the appearance of gold, nor [its] splendor, until the goldsmith, in his wisdom, separates “the dross from the silver,” (Proverbs 25:4) time after time, purification after purification, each time in a different manner, and with each purification it is purified gradually until all the dross is separated from the gold, after which it is recognizable as gold. Similarly, in the case of souls, as a result of the sin of Adam, the first man, good was mixed with evil, and especially with those drops of seed that he gave birth to during those 130 years. We already explained in the discourse regarding sleeping at night and the Bedtime Reading of the Shema that the drops of seed are very valuable and holy, but as they come out, they become mixed with the Klippot. Therefore, they require purification after purification in order to be rectified. In this way, those drops [from Adam] were rectified gradually, until they started being rectified [to the extent that] they revealed the aspect of gold that was within them. This took place during the generation of [the slavery in] Egypt. With this [explanation], you will understand a correct reason for why that harsh, unparalleled slavery was decreed upon them.  Corresponding to how they sinned in the generation of the flood  by destroying their seed, it was decreed upon them, “Every son who is born, you shall throw into the Nile” (Exodus 1:22), similar to the punishment of the Flood itself. Corresponding to how they sinned in the generation of the Dispersion, “Let us make bricks etc.” (Genesis 11:3), it says, “They embittered their lives with mortar and bricks” (Exodus 1:14). I already elaborated about this in other places, in the secret of “Shabbat and [monetary] laws [that] were commanded in Marah”; look there well. [Shmuel said: In another place, I found that they also sinned during the generation of the people of Sedom, but this is not cited here.] However, the reason why the bondage was in Egypt was because it is known that all souls come from the Chassadim and Gevurot that are in the Mo’ach of Da’at (knowledge), upon which the secret of Zivug depends, as the verse says, “Adam knew (Yada) Eve, his wife” (Genesis 4:1), “[and it says], “No man knew her” (Genesis 24:16). It is called Da’at (knowledge) to teach that the drop of Zivug is drawn from there, which is called by an expression of “knowing” (Yedi’ah), as was mentioned. This is especially so in light of the fact that those were the souls of the generation of Moshe our teacher, and we already explained that Moshe was from the aspect of Da’at (knowledge), and similarly, the entire generation was from the aspect of Da’at. However [there was a difference between Moshe and the other people of his generation], because they came out to the Klippot, as they were the drops of seed of the 130 years before Seth was born, but Moshe was from the aspect of Seth himself, as is known. Therefore, it says regarding him, “She saw him, that he is good” (Exodus 2:2). He was not like the other evil drops from Adam, the first man, of the 130 years, because after all of them, Seth was born in his form and his image. On the other hand, the others were in the form of demons and [evil] spirits, so Moshe said about them, “May I not see my evil” (Numbers 11:15); this was already explained elsewhere.
Sermons on Rosh Hashanah Introduction: The concept [behind] the custom practiced by the Ashkenazim on the first day of Rosh Hashanah to go after the afternoon service a little before sunset to the ocean or to a spring or a well of artesian water, which they call Tashlich: Behold, it is a good custom, but it is better if it is outside of the city. One should stand over the edge of the well or the spring and read the three verses of, Who is like You, etc. You will show truth to Jacob, etc., at the end of Micah (7:18-20), which is the aspect of the thirteen rectifications of the supernal beard of the Extended Face [Arikh Anpin]. And with the meaning of the words, one must have in mind how the 13 rectifications of the beard are hinted to, as is known, and where the place of each rectification on the supernal face of the Extended Face is, according to what we explained about the idea of and He passed over (Exodus 34:6) and the thirteen attributes in the weekday morning prayers, see there. And in the Idra Rabba (11:97), they are taught according to the order of [the words of the thirteen attributes of mercy]: Lord, Lord, God merciful and compassionate, etc.: Who is a God like You [corresponds to the] first; forgiving iniquity, the second; and remitting transgression, the third; against the remnant of His inheritance the fourth; Who has not maintained His wrath forever, the fifth; because He desires kindness, the sixth; He will take us back in mercy, the seventh; He will cover up our iniquities, the eighth; You will hurl all our sins into the depths of the sea, the ninth; You will show truth to Jacob, the tenth; kindness to Abraham, the eleventh; as You promised on oath to our fathers, the twelfth; in days gone by, the thirteenth. And when you say, You will hurl all our sins into the depths of the sea, you should have in mind that all of your sins and iniquities be hurled away and that the supernal prosecutor should be hurled into the supernal sea. As that is the reason to say it over the ocean or moving waters. However, you must [also] keep in mind what we explained in the teaching about the thirteen attributes on the ninth rectification that is hinted at in the word to the thousandth generation (Exodus 34:7). And I explained it concerning unifications.
